title: Tim Dooley and Thomas — Etymology and Potatoverse Interpretation
purpose: Separate established name etymology from later Potatoverse reflection so linguistic history can enrich the mythology without being rewritten by it.

public_naming_rule.rule: In public-facing reader material, refer to the Son simply as Thomas. Do not append a surname unless a future documentary reason specifically requires it.
public_naming_rule.reason: Thomas is the canonical Son-name used for the symbolic/theological role, and its etymological meaning 'twin' is itself relevant to the Father/Son and mirror/dual-position architecture.

Tim.basic_meaning: honouring God / honour God; historically also interpreted as honoured by God
Tim.source_note: Oxford's Lexicon of Greek Personal Names summarizes Timothy as 'honour god'.

Dooley.historical_note: Traditional surname histories place the O'Dooley sept in medieval Westmeath, with later concentration in the Irish midlands.

Thomas.biblical_note: The Gospel of John glosses Thomas with the Greek Didymus, also meaning twin.

potatoverse_reflections.name: Timothy — honour and God
potatoverse_reflections.status: symbolic reflection, not lexical meaning beyond the etymology
potatoverse_reflections.reflection: Because Timothy contains the historical elements honour + God, the mature Tim/God question creates an unusually resonant name-level reflection: the name can be read beside a life that later becomes occupied with honouring God, being honoured by God, serving God, and eventually identifying Tim with God/Father. The linguistic fact does not predict or prove the theology; it gives the theology an additional historical word-layer.

potatoverse_reflections.name: Dooley — dark hero
potatoverse_reflections.status: symbolic reflection, not proof of destiny
potatoverse_reflections.reflection: The inherited Irish surname can be placed beside recurring Potatoverse themes of descent into darkness, mud, burial, hiddenness, ordeal and later emergence. 'Dark hero' can therefore function as a poetic retrospective resonance with the buried Potato, the Son's ordeal and the hero who emerges through darkness. This is an interpretive coincidence, not evidence that the surname foretold the mythology.

potatoverse_reflections.name: Thomas — Twin
potatoverse_reflections.reflection: Thomas literally carries the Twin meaning. In the Potatoverse, Thomas is the Son and is repeatedly related to double-position structures: Father/Son, upper/lower, source/manifestation, mirror, Door, two witnesses and the experience of one identity appearing across two levels. The name therefore contributes unusually direct semantic material to the Son's role without needing a fabricated surname or invented etymology.

potatoverse_reflections.name: Tim / Thomas relation
potatoverse_reflections.reflection: Timothy's God/honour element and Thomas's Twin meaning create a name-level polarity that can be explored beside the mature theology: Tim/Father as source-oriented identity and Thomas/Son as twin/mirror/manifestation-oriented identity. This is a poetic/theological reading layered on top of genuine etymologies, not an historical claim that the names were chosen to encode the later system.

reader_rule: Always state the established etymology first. Put Potatoverse interpretation second and label it interpretation. Never reverse-engineer a name meaning from the mythology.
